changes.before: suggests that economic activity has continued to pick up
changes.after: suggests that economic activity has continued to strengthen

changes.before: Businesses are still cutting back on fixed investment, though at a slower pace, and remain reluctant to add to payrolls
changes.after: Business spending on equipment and software appears to be picking up, but investment in structures is still contracting and employers remain reluctant to add to payrolls

changes.before: Although economic activity is likely to remain weak for a time
changes.after: Although the pace of economic recovery is likely to be moderate for a time

changes.before: Financial market conditions have become more supportive of economic growth.
changes.after: While bank lending continues to contract, financial market conditions remain supportive of economic growth.

changes.before: The Federal Reserve expects that amounts provided under the Term Auction Facility will continue to be scaled back in early 2010.
changes.after: The Federal Reserve is in the process of winding down its Term Auction Facility: $50 billion in 28-day credit will be offered on February 8 and $25 billion in 28-day credit will be offered at the final auction on March 8.

changes.before: The Committee will continue to evaluate the timing and overall amounts of its purchases of securities
changes.after: The Committee will continue to evaluate its purchases of securities

Voting against the policy action was Thomas M. Hoenig, who believed that economic and financial conditions had changed sufficiently that the expectation of exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate for an extended period was no longer warranted.

parsed.rationale: The upgraded growth assessment, firm end date for the Term Auction Facility, and Hoenig's dissent against the 'extended period' language tilt the statement hawkish. The core rate guidance and asset-purchase plans are unchanged, so the shift is modest.

suggests that economic activity has continued to strengthen
Business spending on equipment and software appears to be picking up, but investment in structures is still contracting and employers remain reluctant to add to payrolls
Although the pace of economic recovery is likely to be moderate for a time
While bank lending continues to contract, financial market conditions remain supportive of economic growth.

The Federal Reserve is in the process of winding down its Term Auction Facility: $50 billion in 28-day credit will be offered on February 8 and $25 billion in 28-day credit will be offered at the final auction on March 8.
The Committee will continue to evaluate its purchases of securities

Voting against the policy action was Thomas M. Hoenig, who believed that economic and financial conditions had changed sufficiently that the expectation of exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate for an extended period was no longer warranted.
